profile.org_note: Founder-led under co-CEOs Gregg Nelson and Michael Maples, with a COO (Steve Kalmbach, since October 2025) who oversees M&A and the five division presidents; there is no regional layer. Land is sourced by each division (division presidents front the land announcements; Colorado and Southern California have had their own VPs of land acquisition) and cleared through a corporate land committee on which Chief Administrative Officer John Willsie has sat; the CFO is Colin Severn. Capital comes from majority owner Daiwa House, which the company credits for its 'financial support'.
profile.summary: Western U.S. builder with five divisions (Northern, Central and Southern California, Colorado, Washington) and, by its own account, about $1 billion of annual revenue in each of the past two years; majority owned by Japan's Daiwa House since 2020, alongside Daiwa's other U.S. builders Stanley Martin and CastleRock Communities (per ResiClub). It is growing by acquisition (Wathen Castanos 2023, Icon Lending 2025, JK Monarch March 2026) and is buying land outright at a fast clip in 2025-2026 (780 lots in Southern California, 183 finished lots in Oxnard, 589 lots in Visalia and Lemoore, first Washington purchase), which it attributes to Daiwa House's backing. No Texas operations were found: Wathen Castanos is a Central California builder.
